State cooperative contracts need no addendum. **Schools.** The code applies directly to school districts. **List.** None. **Thresholds.** Small-purchase limits are set by each unit's rulemaking authority; the statute has no dollar figure **[mirror]**. Local construction is triggered by an indexed bid limit (2003 bases of $40,000 for building improvements and $125,000 for public works); the 2026 values were not retrieved **[unverified]**. The former $80,000 school-construction trigger was reenacted by 2026 S.B. 164 and should not be assumed to survive ([S.B. 164](https://le.utah.gov/Session/2026/bills/enrolled/SB0164.pdf)).

VT.tier_label: No express statute: interlocal law and local policy
VT.agreement: Schools over $40,000: waiver or own three-bid invitation
VT.excluded: National co-ops not exempt for schools
VT.formal_bid: Schools over $40,000 (advertise or invite three bids); municipalities local
VT.detail: **Authority.** Municipalities have no state bidding mandate; the legislative body sets its own tiers, so cooperative use is a local-policy question **[secondary: VLCT model policy, Dec. 2025]** ([VLCT](https://www.vlct.org/node/346)). The Commissioner of Buildings and General Services may act as a political subdivision's purchasing agent ([29 V.S.A. § 902](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/29/049/00902)). **Schools.** School boards must publicly advertise or invite three or more bids above **$40,000**; the listed exemptions cover joint bidding with other districts and purchases through the Commissioner, **not national cooperatives**, and the Secretary of Education may grant waivers ([16 V.S.A. § 559](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/16/009/00559)). A district buying more than $40,000 through a national co-op therefore needs a waiver, its own three-bid invitation, or a State contract. School construction over $2,000,000 adds prequalification and 60-day advertising. **List.** None. **Thresholds.** Municipal: locally set. Schools: $40,000, with no state micro or quote tier below it. The 2026 amendment (Act 164) was technical and left $40,000 unchanged.

VA.lead_test: Original solicitation stated it was a cooperative procurement for other public bodies
VA.excluded: Architect and engineer services; construction, with listed exceptions
VA.formal_bid: Small-purchase ceilings: $200,000 goods and services; $300,000 construction; $80,000 professional services
VA.detail: **Authority.** Va. Code § 2.2-4304(B) lets any public body (counties, cities, towns, school boards) buy from another public body's contract, including out-of-state, if the original solicitation stated it was a cooperative procurement on behalf of other public bodies ([§ 2.2-4304](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/2.2-4304/)). **Conditions.** Architectural and engineering contracts are excluded, as is construction except artificial turf and track, stream restoration, stormwater management, playground installation and, from July 1, 2026, non-structural roofing work on existing facilities. No resolution, notice or savings finding is required. Localities that have adopted alternative procurement policies follow those policies. **Schools.** Same statute. **List.** None. **Thresholds.** A public body may adopt written small-purchase procedures up to **$200,000** for goods and nonprofessional services, **$300,000** for non-transportation construction and **$80,000** for professional services; above those, sealed bidding or competitive negotiation. The statute sets no micro-purchase floor or quote count for local bodies ([§ 2.2-4303](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/2.2-4303/)).

WA.lead_test: Lead public agency followed its own bid law and posted the solicitation online
WA.excluded: Public works piggybacking possible but rare
WA.quotes: Schools: three quotes, $40,000 to $75,000; counties: vendor list, $10,000 to $50,000
WA.formal_bid: Schools over $75,000 (public works $100,000); counties $50,000; smaller cities over $40,000
WA.detail: **Authority.** RCW 39.34.030 (Interlocal Cooperation Act) is the piggyback statute. Under the State Auditor's reading, a public agency's bid obligations are satisfied when the awarding public agency complied with its own statutory requirements and posted the solicitation online; the statute text itself could not be loaded, so this rests on agency guidance ([SAO guide](https://www.sao.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2023-05/Piggybacking-under-Washington-state-law.pdf)). The host agency may be anywhere in the United States ([MRSC](https://mrsc.org/Explore-Topics/procurement/basics/Piggybacking)). **Conditions.** A **signed interlocal agreement** before use; the lead agency followed its own bid law; the awarding entity is a public agency, a point to verify for cooperatives. A co-op membership agreement may serve as the interlocal agreement. Public works piggybacking is legally possible but rare. **Schools.** Same authority (inference). **List.** None; the Auditor does not pre-approve cooperatives. **Thresholds.** School districts: under **$40,000** no state requirement; $40,000 to **$75,000**, three quotes; over $75,000, sealed bids; public works formal at $100,000 ([RCW 28A.335.190](https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/Law/RCWPDF/RCW%20%2028A%20TITLE/RCW%20%2028A.335%20%20CHAPTER/RCW%20%2028A.335%20.190.pdf)). A 2026 bill to raise these appears not to have passed. Counties: sealed bids at **$50,000**, with a vendor-list process from $10,000 ([RCW 36.32.245](https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/law/RCW/RCW%20%2036%20%20TITLE/RCW%20%2036%20.%2032%20%20CHAPTER/RCW%20%2036%20.%2032%20.245.htm)). Cities: public works bids over $75,500 (single craft) or $150,000 (multiple); purchases over $40,000 for smaller cities and towns; larger cities set their own ([MRSC City Bidding Book](https://mrsc.org/explore-topics/procurement/basics/city-bidding-book)). The small works roster limit is $350,000 through December 31, 2026, then $530,000.

WV.tier_label: Partial: one class of buyer, or reach unclear
WV.no_competition: Counties $15,000 or less; schools under $5,000 [currency unconfirmed]
WV.quotes: Schools: three verbal quotes $5,000 to $10,000; three written to $25,000 [currency unconfirmed]
WV.formal_bid: Counties above $15,000; construction over $50,000; schools $50,000 sealed; municipalities by ordinance
WV.detail: **Authority.** No express local piggyback statute. Local governments rely on the interlocal statute, W. Va. Code § 8-23-3 **[secondary: vendor flyer; official text not fetched]** ([flyer](https://www.inceptia.org/PDF/VG/Cooperative%20Purchasing_WestVirginia_021920.pdf)), and on local bidding rules: municipalities decide by ordinance whether bidding is required ([§ 8-12-10](https://code.wvlegislature.gov/8-12-10/)) and county commissions adopt their own procedures ([§ 7-1-11](https://code.wvlegislature.gov/7-1-11/)). **Schools.** State Board Policy 8200 permits purchases from "a legitimate government purchasing cooperative" whose bidding meets the policy, with justification on file **[mirror: 2012 text]** ([Policy 8200](https://regulations.justia.com/resources/v2024100900/wv/admin/2024/126-202-6.pdf)). The Department of Education's 2025 guidance says construction may not be procured directly from a cooperative contract ([WVDE slides](https://wvde.us/sites/default/files/2025-07/8200%20Revision..7.8.25.pdf)). **List.** No registry; Policy 8200 names example cooperatives. **Thresholds.** Counties: open market at **$15,000** or less, competitive bids above. Municipalities: set by ordinance. Construction for all local bodies and school boards: bids above **$50,000** ([§ 5-22-1](https://code.wvlegislature.gov/5-22-1/)). School boards under the 2012 Policy 8200 text: under $5,000 no bids; $5,000–$10,000 three verbal quotes; $10,000–$25,000 three written bids; $25,000–$50,000 advertisement; $50,000+ sealed bids. A pending revision described in July 2025 would set the competitive threshold at $10,000; adoption was not confirmed, so the school tiers are **[currency unconfirmed]**.

WI.tier_label: Partial: one class of buyer, or reach unclear
WI.agreement: Interstate cooperation agreements go to the attorney general
WI.excluded: Reach to a vendor contract of another government unresolved
WI.formal_bid: Public construction over $25,000 (cities and towns); counties and villages not read
WI.detail: **Authority.** Wis. Stat. § 66.0131(2) lets any local governmental unit "make purchases from another unit of government, including the state or federal government, without the intervention of bids" ([§ 66.0131](https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/statutes/66.0131)). Whether that reaches a purchase from a private vendor under another government's contract is not answered by the text read. Formal cooperation agreements with other states' municipalities must be submitted to the attorney general ([§ 66.0303](https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/statutes/66.0301)). **Schools.** Districts may make intergovernmental contracts; the common statement that Wisconsin has no general school bidding statute is **[unverified]**. **List.** None. **Thresholds.** Cities: public construction over **$25,000** to the lowest responsible bidder, with notice from $5,000 **[mirror]** ([§ 62.15](https://law.justia.com/codes/wisconsin/chapter-62/section-62-15/)). Towns: the same $5,000 and $25,000 tiers, covering materials and supplies as well ([§ 60.47](https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/statutes/60.47)). County and village statutes were not read **[unverified]**. No quote tier found.

WY.tier_label: No express statute: interlocal law and local policy
WY.lead_test: Schools must independently meet their own bid rules
WY.excluded: Co-op contract does not replace school bids
WY.formal_bid: City and town improvements over $75,000; schools publish a call at $50,000; counties not found
WY.detail: **Authority.** No express local piggyback statute was found. Participation rests on the general cooperation statute, W.S. 16-1-101, which covers cooperation with other states' entities but does not mention purchasing **[secondary: vendor flyer]** ([Inceptia Wyoming flyer](https://www.inceptia.org/PDF/VG/Cooperative%20Purchasing_Wyoming_021920.pdf)). The municipal bid statute has no cooperative exemption **[mirror, 2025 code]** ([W.S. 15-1-113](https://law.justia.com/codes/wyoming/title-15/chapter-1/article-1/section-15-1-113/)). **Schools.** W.S. 21-3-110(a)(viii) says a district "shall independently meet the requirements" of the bidding paragraph even when buying through a cooperative services board, so a co-op contract does not replace the district's own bids (read through a legislative staff memo, August 2025) ([LSO memo](https://wyoleg.gov/InterimCommittee/2025/SSF-2025082009-01_SchoolFacilitiesProcurementRequirements.pdf)). **List.** None. **Thresholds.** Cities and towns: advertised bids for public improvements above **$75,000**; new automobiles and trucks must be advertised regardless of cost. School supplies and materials: competitive bids over **$25,000**; published call for bids at **$50,000**. School capital construction: published bids over $50,000. County thresholds were **not found**; 2026 session changes were not checked.
